english_text: in writing . - This regulation is a step in the right direction as it creates an EU set of rights for bus passengers . We also oppose the force majeure clause exempting carriers from the obligation to provide accommodation for passengers in case of cancellations or delays if these are caused by severe weather conditions or major natural disasters , as it can set a precedent for other EU passenger rights legislation . Even though this is not a triumph , it is an improvement , especially for travellers with disabilities and reduced mobility . We managed to ensure non-discriminatory access conditions , disability-related training for the staff of carriers and terminal authorities who deal directly with passengers and compensation for damage or loss of mobility equipment on all routes , regardless of distance . Keeping that in mind , and with a view to creating a harmonised EU set of rights for all passengers , we did not oppose the agreement and abstained in the final vote .
